_README: Filings whose XBRL is itself scaled by a power of ten -- the filer's own numbers, not a parse bug.
Our parsers divide raw rupees by 1e7 and are CORRECT; the source file carries every monetary tag
at 10^k times its true value (BATAINDIA 20190630 std: FinanceCosts 313510000000 vs the same day's
consolidated filing 313510000 -- identical after /1000). `decimals` is NOT a usable signal:
digits-|decimals| == 4 in the broken filings AND the good ones, because the filer derives it from
the broken value.
DETECTION IS NOT AUTOMATABLE, which is why this is a REVIEWED LEDGER and not a heuristic.
A naive '50x the symbol's own median' test flags 268 cells of which ~198 are REAL: company
collapses (JETAIRWAYS), holding-co shells whose standalone is ~0 (BINANIIND, ROLTA), mergers
(ABCAPITAL's 2025 ABFL merger), one-off land sales (SIL Mar-22: rev 429.97 -> op 212.44 is a
textbook ~49% land-sale margin), licensing income (SPARC Mar-26: rev 1853.22 - op 1772.94 = 80.28
of cost, exactly its normal quarterly cost base), and recurring dividends (MAHSCOOTER spikes every
SEPTEMBER -- the annual Bajaj dividend). Auto-'correcting' any of those DELETES REAL DATA, which is
the same trap the ORFO rule fell into (DATA_RUNBOOK 11).
Each k below is ANCHORED, in order of strength: (a) the filing's own YTD minus the quarter must
equal the earlier quarters of that FY, which are known from DIFFERENT filings -- IRCTC, GAEL,
GRAPHITE and TTML come out at EXACTLY 100.000; (b) the same company's other-basis filing for the
same quarter, filed minutes apart; (c) adjacent quarters, only where exactly one power of ten fits.
Applied at PARSE time by build_revop.py + build_fundamentals.py (keyed on `file`, so a full rebuild
stays clean), and to the live JSONs once by apply_scale_fix.py (guarded on `was_*`, so it is
idempotent). Re-detect suspects with detect_scale_errors.py; add an entry only with a real anchor.
